title: Final recommendations
text: Final recommendations A practical synthesis for clinicians. Key clinical lessons drawn from all chapters of this volume:

title: Diagnosis is always the second step, not the first
text: Before diagnosing a mental disorder, always: Exclude medical causes — particularly new onset after age 40–50, acute presentation, atypical profile, somatic symptoms, hormonal changes; Check substance use — covert substance component in 30% of cases; Ask trauma history with open questions — complex PTSD and personality disorders are often the result of trauma, but trauma history does not emerge without screening. ICD-

title: Psychotherapy — first choice in most cases
text: Central message of the ICD-11 era: Psychotherapy effectiveness is confirmed, at least equal to pharmacotherapy, superior in many disorders: Mild-moderate depression — CBT, IPT equivalent to SSRIs; In anxiety disorders — CBT first-line; In OCD — ERP is essential; SSRIs adjunctive; In PTSD — TF-CBT, EMDR first-line; Personality Disorders — DBT, MBT, TFP — more effective than pharmacotherapy; In eating disorders — CBT-E

title: Principle of minimum effective dose
text: Start low, increase slowly; Reaching the lowest effective dose and staying on it; Avoid excessive polypharmacy — especially in the elderly, in comorbidity, and in personality disorders; Discontinuation or dose reduction also requires knowledge — SSRIs must not be stopped abruptly; benzodiazepines should be gradually tapered.

title: Working with culture and context
text: In the Azerbaijani context: Somatic presentation is widespread — depression and anxiety call for active screening in primary care; Stigma and privacy — visits to a psychiatrist are kept confidential; working in primary care or internal medicine settings is effective; Family system is strong — family involvement in treatment is a major resource; Religious and cultural beliefs — should be taken into account, but not tu

title: Screening should be standard in primary care
text: The main screening tools should be routinely applied in primary care: PHQ-9 — depression (at every medical visit); GAD-7 — anxiety; AUDIT — alcohol use; EPDS — perinatal women; C-SSRS — suicide risk. Investments should be made in tools translated and validated into Azerbaijani.

title: Assessment of suicide risk
text: Active inquiry at every psychiatric interview: Have you had thoughts about death or ending your life recently? Concrete plan, means? Previous attempts? Risk factors: Previous attempts (strongest predictor); History of suicide in the family; How close the plan is to being carried out, and how specific it is; Access to means; Substance use, depression, BPD, psychosis; Acute stressor, loss. Intervention: Safety plan; Re

title: Comorbidity is the rule, not the exception
text: In mental disorders comorbidity is the norm: Depression + anxiety — 60% comorbid; PTSD + depression — 50%+; Personality disorder + depression/anxiety/substance — 80%+; Autism + ADHD — 50%; Eating disorder + depression + trauma — typical triad. The treatment plan must cover every comorbidity — treating the main disorder alone is often not enough.

title: Age and developmental stage must be considered
text: Mental disorder in a child — parent and context are crucial; medication plays a smaller role, psychotherapy and family work a larger one; Adolescent — identity development, early intervention critical; Adult — work, family, social function; Older adults — comorbid medical illnesses, polypharmacy, cognitive impairments; dementia versus depression requires special attention.

title: Multidisciplinary team — the foundation of effective clinical work
text: In complex cases: Psychiatrist; Psychologist / psychotherapist; Social worker; Medical physician (comorbidities); Family members (with consent); People at school or at work (when the patient is a child). Developing this structure in Azerbaijan — a strategic priority.

title: Attention to your own health
text: Psychiatric work carries a high emotional load; this is the nature of the profession. Burnout, secondary trauma, compassion fatigue are real risks for the clinician. Supervision and collegial consultation; Individual psychotherapy; Healthy lifestyle; Knowing your limits — you cannot save all patients.
